manifests.title: System representation triangle
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: Solve y=2x+1 and y=-x+7. Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: (2,5).
manifests.learnerOutcome: Interpret a system solution as an input-output point satisfying every equation and solve two-variable systems graphically and algebraically.

manifests.title: Line solution-count gallery
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Choose graphing, substitution, or elimination from the visible structure and verify the ordered pair in every equation. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Interpret a system solution as an input-output point satisfying every equation and solve two-variable systems graphically and algebraically.

manifests.title: Method-choice map
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is accepting a point that satisfies only one equation. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Interpret a system solution as an input-output point satisfying every equation and solve two-variable systems graphically and algebraically.

manifests.title: Nonlinear intersection gallery
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: Solve y=x^2 and y=2x-1. Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: (1,1).
manifests.learnerOutcome: Solve systems involving lines, quadratics, circles, rational, exponential, or other nonlinear functions and interpret all real intersections.

manifests.title: Substitution workflow
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Substitute an isolated equation, solve the resulting one-variable equation, recover the other coordinate, and check every candidate. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Solve systems involving lines, quadratics, circles, rational, exponential, or other nonlinear functions and interpret all real intersections.

manifests.title: Repeated root as tangency
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is listing only x-values instead of complete intersection points. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Solve systems involving lines, quadratics, circles, rational, exponential, or other nonlinear functions and interpret all real intersections.

manifests.title: Layered half-planes
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: x,y≥0, x+y≤10, 2x+y≤14. Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: Vertices (0,0),(0,10),(4,6),(7,0).
manifests.learnerOutcome: Graph simultaneous inequalities, identify feasible regions, and interpret boundaries and vertices.

manifests.title: Boundary inclusion
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Graph each boundary, shade the correct side, include contextual constraints, find vertices, and evaluate an objective when requested. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Graph simultaneous inequalities, identify feasible regions, and interpret boundaries and vertices.

manifests.title: Vertex objective table
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is using the union of regions instead of their overlap. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Graph simultaneous inequalities, identify feasible regions, and interpret boundaries and vertices.

manifests.title: Three-plane gallery
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: Solve x+y+z=6,x-y+z=2,x+y-z=0. Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: (1,2,3).
manifests.learnerOutcome: Solve and classify three-variable linear systems and interpret their solutions as intersections of planes.

manifests.title: Elimination ladder
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Eliminate one variable from two equation pairs, solve the reduced system, and back-substitute. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Solve and classify three-variable linear systems and interpret their solutions as intersections of planes.

manifests.title: Parameterized solution line
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is performing elimination on only one pair and stopping with insufficient information. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Solve and classify three-variable linear systems and interpret their solutions as intersections of planes.

manifests.title: Matrix anatomy
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: Multiply [[1,2],[0,3]] by [[4],[5]]. Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: [[14],[15]].
manifests.learnerOutcome: Represent rectangular arrays with matrices and perform dimension-compatible addition, scalar multiplication, and matrix multiplication.

manifests.title: Dimension compatibility
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Add corresponding entries, scale every entry, and multiply using row-column dot products when inner dimensions match. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Represent rectangular arrays with matrices and perform dimension-compatible addition, scalar multiplication, and matrix multiplication.

manifests.title: Row-column dot product
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is multiplying corresponding entries instead of using dot products. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Represent rectangular arrays with matrices and perform dimension-compatible addition, scalar multiplication, and matrix multiplication.

manifests.title: System-to-matrix translation
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: Row for x+3z=8 in x,y,z order. Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: [1,0,3|8].
manifests.learnerOutcome: Translate linear systems into augmented matrices and justify elementary row operations as equivalent-system transformations.

manifests.title: Row-operation meanings
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Include zero coefficients, translate each equation into a row, and use row swap, nonzero scaling, or row replacement to preserve the solution set. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Translate linear systems into augmented matrices and justify elementary row operations as equivalent-system transformations.

manifests.title: Forbidden zero scaling
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is changing coefficients without changing the constant term. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Translate linear systems into augmented matrices and justify elementary row operations as equivalent-system transformations.

manifests.title: Echelon staircase
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: Interpret [[1,2|3],[0,0|5]]. Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: No solution.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Use forward elimination to reach row-echelon form and solve by back-substitution.

manifests.title: Forward elimination stages
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Choose a pivot, eliminate below it, move to the lower submatrix, and back-substitute from the final pivot row. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Use forward elimination to reach row-echelon form and solve by back-substitution.

manifests.title: Terminal row classifier
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is losing the row-operation audit trail in arithmetic clutter. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Use forward elimination to reach row-echelon form and solve by back-substitution.

manifests.title: RREF checklist
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: Consistent 3-variable system with rank 2. Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: One free variable and infinitely many solutions.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Reduce matrices to RREF and interpret pivots, free variables, rank, and consistency directly.

manifests.title: Pivot-free map
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Continue elimination above pivots, identify basic and free variables, and use rank to classify consistent systems. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Reduce matrices to RREF and interpret pivots, free variables, rank, and consistency directly.

manifests.title: Rank classification table
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is calling a matrix reduced before clearing above pivots. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Reduce matrices to RREF and interpret pivots, free variables, rank, and consistency directly.

manifests.title: Determinant as area scale
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: det [[1,2],[2,4]]. Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: 0; singular.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Compute and interpret determinants, identify singular matrices, and solve suitable systems with inverse matrices.

manifests.title: Singular collapse
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: For [[a,b],[c,d]], compute ad-bc; nonzero means invertible and zero means singular. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Compute and interpret determinants, identify singular matrices, and solve suitable systems with inverse matrices.

manifests.title: Inverse verification
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is attempting to divide by a zero determinant. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Compute and interpret determinants, identify singular matrices, and solve suitable systems with inverse matrices.

manifests.title: Basis-vector explorer
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: A=[[2,1],[0,3]], apply to (4,-1). Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: (7,-3).
manifests.learnerOutcome: Interpret matrices as transformations of vectors and construct a complete multivariable model using equations, inequalities, and matrices.

manifests.title: Transformation gallery
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Read the column images, express an input vector as a basis combination, and form the same combination of output columns. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Interpret matrices as transformations of vectors and construct a complete multivariable model using equations, inequalities, and matrices.

manifests.title: Multivariable model pipeline
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is switching the row and column interpretations halfway through a model. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Interpret matrices as transformations of vectors and construct a complete multivariable model using equations, inequalities, and matrices.
